I wish to bring another matter to the minister's attention. The evidence submitted at the inquiry in connection with the post office at St. Ann's, Ontario, was given to the house, and I want to make a few observations in that connection. There were about 105 pages of evidence and correspondence. I notice in the evidence that the building which was abandoned was in much better condition than the one to which they went. The new premises were not as clean, nor was the accommodation in a general way as good. Moreover, something must be said about the calibre of the four or five witnesses who tried to substantiate the charge against the previous postmaster. I know a considerable number of the citizens including nine or ten of the most responsible men in that community who testified on behalf of the previous postmaster. Petitions were circulated to which nearly eighty-five per cent of the community subscribed one hundred per cent in favour of the former postmaster. I have read all this evidence carefully, and I wonder whether the Postmaster General has gone thoroughly into this case. Before I get through I am going to bring to his attention something which should convince him of the absolute injustice of the action that was taken 31111-814
in this particular case. I refer particularly to the calibre of the men who testified against the former postmaster. I wonder whether the minister carefully reviewed all the evidence that was brought down in the return asked for and whether, having reviewed it, he is of opinion that any charge had been made out against the man who previously held the office. Does he not think it was absolutely a case of discrimination?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: As soon as my hon. friend mentioned this case I sent for the file. It has only just come in and I have not had an opportunity of looking it over, but I think I know the evidence probably as well as he does. I read it all and considered it carefully, and I did so because a special request was made to me by the postmaster's counsel, an eminent lawyer from Toronto. I went over the evidence with him and these are the circumstances as I recall them. In August, 1935, the man who had been postmaster there for a number of years-a gentleman named Snyder, who bore an excellent reputation in the community but wrho was certainly not as popular with the Liberal party as with the Conservatives, for he was a strong Conservative-became assistant postmaster, the post office being given to his son shortly before the election. For the father's actions in the post office, the son, who was the postmaster, was responsible. The investigation was held by a competent young man whom the hon. member for the riding will know-a Mr. Bench-and the evidence disclosed that a number of persons had stated that he had repeatedly spoken very strongly in favour of his particular political party, and that he did so in the store in which the post office was held, and in the presence of the son, who was the postmaster. The finding was that he was guilty of political partisanship. There was no question about it. My hon. friend after reading the evidence must admit that there was evidence of partisanship on which the commissioner who heard the witnesses could quite properly find that the man had been guilty of partisanship. That was the finding. I was asked to consider it very carefully; I went over all the evidence with counsel for the postmaster, and I would say to my hon. friend that after reading the evidence there was no course left for me but to accept the finding of the commissioner.

I wonder
whether my hon. friend thinks that I interviewed the people who gave evidence, or had an opportunity of judging them as the commissioner who heard the evidence had. The commissioner, a gentleman of repute, a barrister of high standing at the Ontario bar, heard these witnesses; he came to his own conclusion, and I am satisfied that the correct thing to do in view of his finding was what the department did. It is not a pleasant thing to dismiss a man who is getting up in years and who has served the office well in the past, with the exception that he was a bit partisan at election times. But when a change is made just prior to the election, the office handed from the father to the son, and the son is the postmaster and the father the assistant, then I do not think my hon. friend will claim that, when a complaint is made and the man who hears the evidence finds that the father was guilty of political partisanship in the office and to the knowledge of the son, and that under the law he should be dismissed, it would be fair that that postmaster should be retained. After all, this is a business. You cannot have the postmaster irritating and annoying people who are compelled to come into the store where the post office is situated to do business when an election is pending. There are, of course, certain ridings in which political feeling runs higher than in others-I am not saying my hon. friend's riding is one of those, but his party has been very fortunate in that riding for a long time. I think he is not being quite fair to the people who gave evidence there to t'he effect that almost every time they went into the store this assistant postmaster said something to them about the demerits of the Liberal party and the merits of the Conservative party, to contend that they should have to put up with that. In the past the practice has been to accept the finding of the commissioner, and I venture to say that in no case has more care been given to making sure that that finding was right than in this case.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT

A commissioner is sworn; evidence is given on both sides, and given under oath. My hon. friend the member for Lincoln (Mr. Lockhart) takes the view that perhaps some of the witnesses were not of the same calibre as the people who gave evidence the other way. If that was so, I would point out that counsel who acted for this gentleman was at fault, on the basis as laid down by my hon. friend, in not proving or giving evidence of bad character. That not having been done, the com-

Supply-Post Office
missioner was bound by the evidence, and no matter how many petitions came in they did not come before him, they were not signed under oath. If such factors as this should enter into an inquiry, why should they not apply to proceedings in the magistrates' courts, in the county courts, in the supreme court? You can get lots of people to sign petitions against people being hanged, but that does not prove that they were not guilty. If citizens of my hon. friend's riding knew that people of "questionable" character gave evidence, they should have given evidence of that "questionable" character, so that the commissioner, the Postmaster General and his officials could have taken that into consideration. In spite of what the minister has said I should like to protest against the change that was made last Christmas season. A few moments ago the minister suggested that the demand came from the larger centres, and he tells us now that it would be quite impossible to give the service if we reverted to the old arrangement. As a matter of fact, we had the old arrangement for a great many years. The postal employees in my city objected very decidedly to the change, in the first place because of the arbitrary way in which the announcement was made. They had no previous indication, I understand, that this change was being made. At times this department has considered the advisability of setting up some sort of joint, councils. It seems to me that whether or not we have such councils, the least that might be done, where a large group of faithful employees such as the postmen are concerned, would be to give due notice of the intention of the department; in fact I think they might have been taken into consultation.
With regard to the deliveries at Christmas, in our childhood we had an old saying, " Christmas comes but once a year." I think everyone feels that the postmen, who>
are serving us very, very faithfully, ought to be allowed to have Christmas day off. Some of them regard Christmas as having a very distinct religious significance. The great majority of them look upon it as a home day, and I do not think, merely because they are government employees, the postmen ought to be deprived of enjoying that one day in the year. A great many of them have very heavy work prior to Christmas; many men have heavy work during Christmas week. I do not object so much to the delivery on New Year's day, which has neither the same religious significance nor the same home traditions and which, outside of perhaps the Scotch community-

Supply-Post Office

mas day. I know that the interests of the general public must be considered. I think I touch a fair cross-section of the community, and among my own friends in various circles I found a good deal of regret expressed because of the action taken by the department. Business men do not want their mail delivered on Christmas day, except under very exceptional circumstances. The people who most enjoy Chirstmas day want other people also to have an opportunity to enjoy themselves. For many years past it has been the practice of the department, and a very good practice too, to send out a warning to the public to post their Christmas mail early. They have fair warning, and if they delay in getting out their Christmas mail I see no reason why the postmen should be penalized. If necessary, an extra force should be put on. I know extra men are put on, but, if necessary, that force could be doubled, in order, that as much mail	as is required	may	be delivered by the day before Christmas.I should also like to say a word with regard to Saturday afternoon. Last	year	I protested in this house against the practice that had grown up	of	frequently having	no delivery for two	or	three days.	Often	a holiday falls on a Monday, which would mean that there would be no delivery from Saturday morning until Tuesday. I think we made a mistake in allowing that practice to develop, because I knew of certain business men who had important mail delayed for two or three days. I suggested that some change should be made in order to remedy that state of affairs. Now the minister has gone altogether too far. He now wants to take away the Saturday half holiday in any case. It would seem to me reasonable that there might be a delivery in certain restricted business districts on Saturday afternoon. I recognize that important mail may have to be delivered at that time, but as far as the general public are concerned, many people now take Saturday afternoon off, and I do not see why the postmen, with the exception of those necessary for the delivery of mail in such restricted areas, should not have their Saturday afternoons free as well. I brought up this matter last year and pleaded that a change should be made so that we would not run through from Saturday until Tuesday without a mail delivery, and because of that fact I now ask the minister not to go quite as far as he has gone and, if possible, to give the great majority of the men their Saturday afternoons off.

But I said it seemed to me to be going altogether too far to proceed to cut out the Saturday holiday for all the men. That had not been
in my mind at all a year ago. I said I thought that in the swing back from what seemed to be a certain easy-going arrangement the Postmaster General had gone too far.
I do think that it might be possible for the majority of the men to be given a half holiday on Saturday, but that in certain restricted business districts a Saturday afternoon service might be given by putting on more men. That is all I said, I wish especially that the Postmaster General would reconsider the Christmas arrangements, so that the postmen would have their Christmas day.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I know how interested the hon. member is on behalf of the people who are engaged in this and other kinds of labour. I hope I am not entirely unsympathetic to those men. We are paying a very substantial sum for the Saturday afternoon service and it is treated as overtime. Formerly, when the Saturday afternoons were taken off, when Christmas was taken off and when New Year's day was taken off, there was no reduction in the pay of the men. When we give the extra service we give overtime to the men who serve. I do not see how there could be any possible objection, and I know that was the view of the people who represented them on the discussions. Of course it is only fair to say that they preferred to get the overtime pay, that they did not want to have the time worked off by somebody other than themselves. However, this time is being worked off, and we are paying a substantial amount for it. We thought we had given fair treatment to the people engaged in the service.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT

I should like to learn from the Postmaster General if he has had a number of protests from business people in Winnipeg with respect to deliveries on Saturday afternoon. That city is perhaps distinguished by the fact that the vast majority of business offices are closed that afternoon. I have had a great many communications from people in the postal service and even more from people in business offices protesting against having their mail fired through a slot in the door only to lie there from Saturday noon until Monday morning.
I was interested, too, in the fact that the minister based his decision in this matter upon investigations conducted in Montreal. It is not very often an hon. member rises to boast of the smaller size of his native city, but, after all, certain conditions which obtain in large centres are not found in the smaller ones, and the absence of those conditions accounts for many of us choosing to live in a smaller city where we believe
Supply-Post Office

working conditions are more favourable and where we may live the type of life we desire.
Throughout my constituency I have not heard any approval of the Saturday afternoon delivery. If there are some in the constituency who like it, at least they have not been vocal. If the minister has heard from them, I should like to know about it. With respect to Christmas delivery may I say that I have lived in Winnipeg for a number of years, during which we did not have Christmas delivery. In Winnipeg I believe we have not experienced any grievous disrupting of the mail service on that account. Very few business offices do any serious business in the few days before Christmas-I have had enough experience to know that; no doubt much of the post office Christmas business is in Christmas cards.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Mr. Chairman, my question may sound peculiar, but I do not find any item, other than this one, under which it could be asked. Are there any rules and regulations governing the sending of anonymous literature through the mail? I refer particularly to literature which may be described as propaganda. I believe there are parcels of literature going through the mail which are really a menace to peace, order and good government. During an election campaign literature must have printed upon it the name of the printer and the name of the party under whose authority the literature is printed. But between elections the mails are used for purposes of propaganda, and on many occasions carry anonymous letters.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: There is a section in the act forbidding the sending of any obscene, immoral or scurrilous communications. The difficulty in connection with anonymous matter is to find out who is sending it in order that he may be brought within the provisions of this section. In the great majority of cases it is practically impossible to find out who is sending this type of mail. The sender usually typewrites his letter; he uses a different type of envelope and paper from that which he is in the habit of using and he mails the letter at a different post office. If his letters reach the point of being scurrilous or obscene or immoral, then the act would apply, but there is no section referring to anonymous matter.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT

I should like to say a word
or two with reference to the delivery of mail by rural mail carriers. I am surprised to hear certain hon. members complaining about getting too much mail service. When a holiday comes on a Monday, as happens in many instances, mail on the rural routes is delivered on the previous Friday and then there is no more delivery until the following Wednesday. This is what happens in many of the rural parts of Manitoba due to train services and other conditions. Such a service is certainly not good, and if this holiday service is going to. be considered a general policy, I think some consideration should be given to the people residing in the rural districts. Where the rural mail carrier is permitted to consider Saturday as a holiday, there is no delivery of mail between Friday afternoon and Wednesday when a holiday falls on Monday.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext:
Mr. Chairman, I do not
want to go quite as far as some hon. members have gone in criticizing the minister, particularly certain hon. members on his own side of the house. I think the remarks of the hon. member for Winnipeg South Centre (Mr. Maybank) express the sentiments of most hon. members with relation to postal employees working on Saturday afternoons and on Christmas day. Why does the minister permit a different condition to exist in one province from that existing in other provinces? The Postmaster General admitted to the hon. member for Winnipeg South Centre that the postmen in the city of Quebec did not have to work on Christmas day. I should think that if the Postmaster General issued a regulation as to the working hours of posties, that regulation should be uniform in all the cities of Canada. The posties of one city should not be privileged over the posties in other cities.
When these estimates were last before the committee, the Postmaster General admitted that a number of young men had been brought in from Newmarket, Aurora and other points within twenty-five miles of Toronto to work as extra postal employees during the rush period. I notice the hon. member for York North (Mr. Mulock) is present, but I

Supply-Post Office
am sorry the hon. member for York West (Mr. Streight) is not. They should be proud of having been able to get positions for so many men in Toronto to the exclusion of unemployed young men in that city. They certainly lowered my prestige. When I was home last Saturday a number of people told me that I did not seem to have any more influence. They had read the Postmaster General's remark and they realized why the young men in my riding were not able to get on at Christmas as extra postal employees. As a matter of fact, I did not try to get any on, but that is actually what happened.
. When I was home, I met a postie who was dressed in a brown uniform. I asked him why he was not dressed like the other posties and he told me he was just on temporarily. I asked him if he had tried his examinations under the civil service, and he told me quite frankly that he had not, that he had come in from North York to go to work. I extend my congratulations to the hon. member for that district on the large number of young men he has been able to place in the city of Toronto. Shortly afterwards I met two other young men who had tried the postal examinations advertised for November 21. I ask the minister if this is the proper way to run a department? The newspapers carriedi a great story about the several hundred additional employees who were to be taken on in the postal service, and examinations were advertised for November 21. These young men went down and tried the examinations, but here we are well into the new year and those who passed are not yet in the service. When the estimates were last before the committee, the minister told us that the said extra employees would be on until perhaps March 1.
In conclusion, I want to say that I endorse every word of objection that has been said with reference to working on Saturday afternoons. This is a new thing as far as Toronto is concerned. I also endorse all the objections made to posties working on Christmas day. I hope the minister will turn over a new leaf. His estimates have been under a good deal of fire, more from his own side of the chamber than from this, and he should consider taking patronage out of his department and turning the appointments back to the civil service commission.

speechtext: Then the ordinary course was not followed, that is the usual procedure between an employer of labour and an accredited association of employees, of taking them into consultation before adopting a new policy in regard to the particular work. It is correct to say that that policy was adopted without consultation with the employees. However, I do not have to labour that point because, from the information I have, the employees' associations are not objecting to continuous service; if there is a difference of opinion it is as to which method should be adopted, a five-day week, or a six-day week with a lay-off for a certain time. In that regard has any definite policy yet been adopted?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: No. The five-day week is another proposition, and I should prefer that my hon. friend would not mix the two matters, because they are not related. The position is this. I think there would be unanimity among all the employees if they, the present employees, got overtime in cash instead of somebody else being taken on to work out the overtime. That, I think, is about the main question between them. But I explained to them that this is being given to people who do not have jobs, and it was thought it was fairer to give this bit of work to someone who was not employed rather than to somebody who already had a job. The employee gets, as my hon. friend understands, a week off for every eleven afternoons that he puts in.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Some time ago I read about a new and improved service between Edmonton and Athabaska. Would the minister explain what that new service is?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I think the hon. member is referring to the service between Edmonton and Lloydminster. We have recently changed from baggage car service to a railway post office between Edmonton and Lloydminster by way of Willingdon.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext:
That is not what I was referring to. I recently read an announcement in the Edmonton press that consideration had been given to a request or that

a request had been made to increase the service between Edmonton and Athabaska. Is there anything in that?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: No. That matter is under consideration, but no decision has been reached.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Before the minister comes to any decision, I should like to tell him about the service that the Peace River country is now receiving. It is not my intention to make a speech this evening about the merits of the Peace River country-I shall do that later on-but I should like to point out that the present population is somewhere around 70,000 and that the only service we get there is two trains a week; that is, we get mail on Tuesdays and Fridays and the rest of the time we have to go without it. I understand that the United Air Transport planes operating out of Edmonton are carrying on a daily service between Edmonton and the town of Grande Prairie, and the department could very well utilize that line to give a more frequent mail service to the residents of the north country. Nowhere else in Canada, no matter how distant it is, are 70,000 people receiving so little attention as we in the Peace River country. This may be due, of course, to the poor efforts of the member for the constituency, but I shall try to remedy that in the near future. I should like the minister to consider seriously what I am saying, because I believe these people are entitled to better mail service than they are receiving. Two years ago the Lesser Slave lake rose to such a degree that at various points it washed out the railroad. There was a time when no mail was delivered for a period of seven or eight days, and even at that, motor boats had to be used to bridge the gaps over various portions of the railway which had been washed out. The service at that time was most unsatisfactory. I am sure the minister, knowing the beautiful climate of that part of the country, is aware that it would be possible to use aeroplanes to a greater extent than at the present time, especially in view of the fact that there is now an established passenger service between Edmonton and Grande Prairie. The people of that country would be grateful to him if he could find it in his heart to help them and to give them the consideration which is due them.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext:
I can assure my hon. friend that that matter, and a great many other requests from people who think they are in almost as bad a position as that in which the people of the Peace River dis-

Supply-Post Office
trict consider themselves to be, are receiving the best attention we can give them.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: If the hon. member for York North (Mr. Mulock) has been successful through the medium of the civil service commission, he is to be complimented. I have been interested in this discussion on dismissals and I can tell the hon. member for Lincoln (Mr. Lockhart) that, as far as I know, the dismissals have not been one-sided, because I know there are cases in my constituency where dismissals have been made without any commission being appointed. It would be interesting to the hon. member for Lincoln and other hon. members to look up the records for the constituency I represent and see how dismissals have been made there. In one instance a man was dismissed merely on the word of a certain gentleman, notwithstanding that the reports all showed that everything had been O.K. throughout. There were no reports that were not perfectly in order; yet this man was dismissed without cause and the secretary of the Conservative association, a man who had held that position for some years, was appointed postmaster. The old postmaster had two girls working for him, one a Liberal and the other a Conservative. When the new postmaster was appointed he dismissed the Liberal girl and kept the Conservative. These dismissals are not by any means all one-sided, and, as I say, the hon. member for Lincoln would find it interesting to look up the record.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: You have asked us to be fair to you, Mr. Chairman, and I suggest that you should be fair to the committee. You saw me on my feet half a dozen times and yet you allowed five other hon. gentlemen to speak. It is hardly fair of you when you expect civility not to show us some in return.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Order.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext:
That is all I am going to say; I am not criticizing you too severely, but I do not want to be jumping up and down like a jack-in-the-box. The hon. member for Davenport (Mr. MacNicol) made some remarks with regard to the eligible list of persons to be appointed as letter carriers and postmen in Toronto. I believe that some two hundred are wanted. The minister says that he has a letter from the civil service commission to the effect that the examination papers have not yet been all read. I have been making inquiries and have been told that the examiners of the civil service commission are really breaking down in health, they are working so hard. Whoever heard of
such a thing around here? Just imagine a man writing an examination last November and the papers not being checked up yet by the great staff they have in the Hunter building! It seems to me their system should be changed or they should be eliminated entirely if they cannot do better.
Speaking of Saturday afternoon deliveries and the delivery on Christmas day and New Year, I am not going to criticize them at all because every city has its own difficulties. In Toronto, if we did not get a Saturday afternoon delivery the service would be poor indeed, and until the Post Office Department decides to give us an up to date service and have the mail that goes out on the train from Montreal or Ottawa as well as the mail coming from the west, sorted and delivered to people resident two or three miles distant from the post office, it is no service at all. If I wrote a letter to my home on Friday and that letter arrived in Toronto at 7.50 Saturday morning, it would not be delivered at my house until Monday morning. We are entitled to better service.
I am not asking men to work on Saturday afternoon, but I submit that there should be some system whereby the morning mail would be sorted and got out before noon. Around King street, Colborne street and Church street there are three or four deliveries before twelve o'clock, though, as some hon. members have said, most of the places there are closed in the afternoon and people do not want deliveries there at that time of day. On the other hand, the outlying districts will get no service at all if they do not get an afternoon delivery on Saturday.
As regards delivery on Christmas day, I have spoken to only two or three of the postmen and they all tell me that they were delighted to deliver mail on Christmas day because the presents came in fast and they went home happy, whereas if they did not deliver mail on Christmas day they would not get as much out of the job. On New Year's day there is not the same demand for service, though the Scotchman from Davenport thinks it is as important. I have to differ with some of my best friends and with the Postmaster General himself at times.
At any rate, the laughing stock of the whole matter is the suggestion that the civil service commission have not been able to examine three or four hundred papers written early in November. It is now the twenty-fourth of February and the papers have not yet all been examined. I am told by the department that the health of the civil service commission examiners is breaking down because they are
Supply-Post Office

working night and day. If you make any complaint to that department you get a long letter from the secretary, Mr. Foran, a letter of three or four pages cleverly written. I have been in this house since 1921 and I have never yet known a friend of mine who wrote an examination, whether he got 96, 98 or 100 per cent to get a job from the civil service commission. Is there not something wrong? I will go so far as to say that half of the jobs advertised are filled before the advertisement reaches us, and it is only a waste of paper because we simply throw these advertisements into the wastepaper basket.
The civil service has become a matter of personal patronage; it is not political patronage, though it might as well be political. I have never seen a service so badly looked after in my life. It is really a scandal, the way in which it is handled. We have many good friends there and we look sometimes for fair treatment, but it seems to me that no matter who it is you get the same treatment, because they say, " Oh, we are all sworn to do so and so." They are sworn to look after themselves and their own friends.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I have been attempting for about an hour to get a word in and now that everyone else has spoken, perhaps I can ask one or two questions. I was wondering, in those cases where a commission is necessary, what procedure is followed in order to have a commissioner appointed.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: The commissioner is appointed on recommendation of the Minister of Justice to council.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Does the civil service commission make a recommendation to the Minister of Justice?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Is the commissioner sometimes a partisan or is he always independent? An hon. member here said that a partner of the party who laid the complaint was appointed as commissioner. That does not look good to me. I was wondering whether these commissioners are partisan or whether they are independent.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: The department recommends obtaining the best man possible, to make the investigation, and I have great faith in the Minister of Justice appointing nobody who is not thought to be competent for that office. Then, of course, the commissioner who is appointed under the Inquiries Act is sworn to do his duty without fear, favour or affection.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext:
Do these commissioners get any remuneration in the way of travelling or living expenses or per diem allowance?
[Mr. Spence.J

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: They do; they get travelling expenses and send in a bill for their time, and that is taxed by the justice department also.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I should like to know whether any new post offices were established during 1936, and if so, how many in each province.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Does my hon. friend refer to the calendar year?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Calendar year or fiscal year.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext:
My hon. friend will find in the Postmaster General's report for the year ended March 31, 1936, the new post offices established in that year. The report for this year of course is not yet made. But if he will look at page 6 of the report for 1935-36, he will see the total number of offices established from April 1, 1935, to March 31, 1936, was 148. The number closed in the same period was sixty-one. The number opened during the period November 1, 1935, to December 31, 1936, by provinces is as follows:
Nova Scotia	 6
Prince Edward Island	 0
New Brunswick	 14
Quebec	 79
Ontario	 53
Manitoba	 9
Saskatchewan	 30
Alberta	 17
British Columbia	 16

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Were any rural mail routes established in the same period?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I cannot at the moment give with the same definiteness the number of mail routes. There were some new routes established, some improvements to the services, that is in the frequency of mails in a number of post offices. I could not give that up to date, but I could get it for my hon. friend if he wishes.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext:
May I make a suggestion with regard to the extra help that will be required in the larger cities at the coming Christmas? Last year we provided for a veterans' assistance commission, whose duty was to help solve the problem of unemployed veterans in Canada. I believe that there are 33,000 unemployed veterans who have answered the questionnaire sent out by that commission, and over half of that number are employable. In addition to the commission, there are strong honorary local committees, in ten cities at least, perhaps more by this time. These men are doing their best to get work for these unemployed veterans, and my suggestion to the minister is that he adopt a

Supply-Post Office
policy of giving this veterans' assistance commission and also these honorary local committees the first choice in the placing of men required for extra post office work at Christmas time. If he will do that, and particularly if he will announce such a policy shortly, it will give great encouragement to these local committees and also to>
the unemployed veterans, and might go a long way towards making the veterans' assistance commission a success.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: There were 817 returned soldiers engaged for this work for the last Christmas rush in Toronto alone. That is 204 more than were engaged the year before. Every returned soldier who was on the eligible list and was available and suitable for the employment was taken. I might give a statement of how these employees are selected. Returned soldiers with dependents get the preference; next, civilians with dependents; next, returned soldiers without dependents, and, last, civilians without dependents.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I realize that that has been the rule, and I am not complaining particularly about what happened last Christmas, because I do not know. But now this veterans' assistance commission has been set up. and they are dealing with the problem of the unemployed returned men-I emphasize the word "unemployed"-it would help a great deal if the department would make a new rule in regard to veterans, and would go first to the veterans' assistance commission, and to the honorary local committees which are serving under that commission, for a list of returned men who are to get the preference.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I think the veterans' organization is nearly always consulted by the postmaster in any district where there is any large number of soldiers being taken on. But I shall make further inquiries and give the matter my best consideration.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: The veterans' assistance commission has been appointed recently. It was not in a position to furnish names last Christmas, but I believe it will be this coming Christmas. I am sure the Minister of Pensions will endorse my suggestion.

speakerposition: Minister of Pensions and National Health
maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I am wondering why my hon. friend is in such a hurry to get their reports, when he says they have only started to work. Not long ago he kept me here three hours to get an interim report.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext:
Well, they seem to be
working very slowly; I am trying to help
the minister out. I think he should be more grateful.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: May I ask the Postmaster General if he could give the total number of employees in the Toronto district, both returned men and general, during the Christmas rush? Also is it possible to get the names and addresses of these temporary employees to see whether they reside in Toronto? There seems to be a kind of inference that a considerable number came from outside Toronto, and if we could get the addresses that matter might be cleaned up

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I do not think there will be any difficulty in getting the names at any rate.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: And addresses; the addresses are very important.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: If the postmaster has kept the addresses, I shall be glad to have them furnished to my hon. friend.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I do not wish to hold up the vote unnecessarily, but I should like to come back to the very important matter of the balance sheet. On a previous occasion the minister said the surplus would be a littile more than $3 000,000. In the course of his remarks on that occasion he stated that this year the cost of the franking privilege would amount to $1,001,000. I should like to know why the cost of the franking privilege during the first year in office of the Liberal party should increase from $750,000 to $1,001,000, or by approximately fifty per cent.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: That is for both incoming and outgoing mail. Of course there has been a general increase in the business of the departments of the government, and I can only say that the members, who are largely responsible for the use of the franking privilege, decide how much mail they shall send. Of course there are also certain departmental documents that are sent out, and I suppose the departments decide that. I could get my hon. friend the particulars.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Am I correct in assuming that $1,001,000 is the correct figure, while the amount of $750,000 stated in the annual report is an approximate figure?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: The $750,000 is an accurate estimate made, as I understand it, by actual measurement of the mail going out from here. The $1,001,000 includes the mail coming in.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext:
My next question deals with the matter of the expense in connec-
Supply-Post Office

tion with the savings bank branch of the post office. The amount stated in the return is $60,000, while the amount mentioned by the minister is $80,000, an increase of $20,000.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I am told that this increase is attributable to an increase in the number of accounts and the general overhead expenses.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Can the minister inform the committee as to the amount of money that was actually paid to the postmasters in connection with their work in the savings bank branch?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I do not have it just at hand but I shall have it in a moment.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I have another question. Is the amount charged for heating assumed by the Post Office Department or by some other department? What I should like to get is a correct balance sheet for the Post Office Department.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: The estimate given was prepared, I understand with a great deal of labour and care, by the Public Works department.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext:
Is that expenditure
assumed by the Public Works department?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Yes.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I have just two more short questions, and then I am through. What rate of interest is allowed on deposits in the post office savings bank?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I understand it is two per cent.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Could the minister give me the net profit derived from the operations of the post office savings bank last year?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: The point I am trying to make is that if the post office savings bank costs the government $80,000 and the profits are less than $80,000, I cannot understand why the government should maintain that branch. Why not leave the business to the chartered banks? I should like to get the information if it is available.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext:
I think I can explain to my hon. friend just how this works out. This money is paid into the consolidated revenue fund. The finance depart-
[Mr. Marshall.J
ment has the use of the money. Certain fees are paid to the postmasters for services rendered in taking in the deposits, but the Post Office Department receives no pay as a department. This policy was originated with a view to encouraging thrift by inducing people to deposit savings in this bank, which has the security of the dominion at its back. The offices are there; we have the facilities with which to give the service, and I say very frankly that I think the public should avail themselves of that privilege to a much greater extent than has been the case up to the present. A good rate has always been paid on deposits, and the dominion has had the use of the money at that rate.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: How many branches are there in the dominion?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext:
If my hon.
friend will look at page 11 of the last report, that is. the report for the year ended March 31, 1936, he will see all the details as the situation existed at that time. There have been some changes since then. At that time the number of post offices transacting business had increased from 1.272 to 1,282 and the amount on deposit was a little over $22,000,000. The number of depositors is given, together with the number of new accounts issued.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Mr. Chairman-

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Mr. Chairman-

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: The hon. member for Peel has the floor.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: On a point of order, Mr. Chairman, the hon. member who was given the floor is not speaking from his proper seat in this house.

speakerposition: Deputy Speaker and Chair of Committees of the Whole of the House of Commons
maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: The point of order is not well taken in committee.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext:
Mr. Chairman. I came down to this seat from the back benches with the idea of finding out whether there was anything in the suggestion made by the hon. member for Parkdale (Mr. Spence) with respect to being noticed by the chair when one desires to ask a question. After sitting here a moment or so I have a suggestion to make. I believe money would be well spent to provide rear-vision mirrors for hon. members sitting in the front seats, so that they will have an opportunity of seeing those on the rear benches who have stood up and wish to speak. Seriously, I should like to learn from the minister whether or not the advertising done by the Post Office Depart-

Supply-Post Office
ment to avoid a Christmas rush of mail has had the effect of equalizing the traffic. If not, at what time during the Christmas season does the peak load come?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: My advice is that for years advertising has been carried on urging all persons sending extra mail to mail it as early as possible. Apparently in Canada we have not yet formed the habit of mailing early, as it is done in the old country. I am told the campaign over there has succeeded much better than has the one in Canada. I believe, however, that, in view of the large amount of mail handled, the advertising did some good last Christmas. I cannot express too strongly the wisdom of mailing as early as possible.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: How many temporary employees were taken on in Hamilton during the Christmas and New Year rush?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext:
I cannot
answer directly, but I could get the information from the postmaster at Hamilton. Probably there will be returns in the office here in Ottawa.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: And the number of returned men?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Yes; I should be glad to get the information and send it to the hon. member.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Would the minister tell me the number of postal notes or post office orders issued on Christmas day in Hamilton? I can furnish the information, if he does not have it.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Then I wonder why the hon. member asks me.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I was wondering whether the minister knew.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: No.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: As we are aware, Hamilton post office was open Christmas day. I would suppose the wicket at which the postal notes would be handed out would be attended by possibly two employees. The fact is that only one postal note was issued, and that about five o'clock on Christmas afternoon.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext:
I wish to correct a reference made by the hon. member for Halifax (Mr. Finn) in a discussion which took place earlier in the evening. It was a question as to general standing in the community; I do not wish the inference to go out that it was a question of character.
May I say to the minister that I appreciate the explanation he gave in connection with
the evidence. Now that the dismissal has been made, from the explanation given by the minister I conclude that it was made because of the indiscretion of the father who was seventy-two years of age, and that there is nothing against the present holder of the post office. That was the impression I got. The indiscretion of the father, as I understand it, seemed to be the important point. Am I correct ?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I would say that the postmaster is liable for the indiscretion of his assistant in a case like this.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: That is a terrible principle.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: The evidence went to show that these discussions took place on several occasions in the presence of the postmaster, in the post office or the store of which the post office formed a part, and without any objection from the postmaster.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: But the point I am raising is this: The charge of indiscretion was brought against the assistant postmaster. No charge of any kind whatever was brought against the postmaster himself.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Does the hon. member think it was very discreet for the postmaster to stand by and allow his father, who is his assistant, to talk politics to the people coming into the office? If that is being discreet, then he was guilty of no indiscretion.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: But the new postmaster appointed was not involved in any way, was he, with the exception of the indiscretion of allowing his father, a man of seventy-two years, to discuss matters?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I have the return before me; I do not recall anything else, other than attending meetings.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext:
I should like to inquire about the trans-Canada mail, from the east to Vancouver. Are the contracts held by both railways or by one of them? For instance, are the mails to Vancouver connecting with the boat service handled by both railways? I know the Canadian National Railways, which pass through a large section of my constituency, carry no mails. The result is that the mail goes to Vancouver and then back up through some other service, perhaps by way of an electric railway or some other means. If the contracts are held by one road, for how many years has that been the condition?
Supply-Post Office

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext:
The rates
are set by order in council. There is no definite term in the contract.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: No term in the contract?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: No; each railway is utilized to the extent the department thinks it can best be utilized to the advantage of the service.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext:
I understand that for a
number of years the mails have been carried over one road.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: In some cases that is true.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: The other road, the junior one, has not had the opportunity to carry them.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: That is true in regard to some of the services.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: And that will be continued, I suppose?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext:
Well, it is
hard to say what may happen.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I do not wish unnecessarily to delay the passage of the item. I believe the district of Montreal has been fairly well treated by the Post Office Department. Outside the occasional instance of a dog biting a postman, and some other minor incidents, we have fairly good service. However, there is one point I should like to bring to the attention of the minister. I have before me a file almost a quarter of an inch thick detailing my effort to secure a post office box on the corner of Grey and Western avenues in Notre Dame de Grace in the district of Mount Royal. I believe delay is being caused through the inaction of the postal authorities in Montreal. I bring the matter to the attention of the Postmaster General so that he may stir them up to a little quicker action, and have the box placed in the location I have indicated for the convenience of the public living in the immediate vicinity. I hope the minister will give the matter some consideration, and ascertain where the delay has been occasioned. If instructions have been given for the placing of the box, so much the better.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I shall have the matter looked into. I cannot say I have given personal attention to it, but I am strongly of the impression that possibly something can be done.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext:
Is the department contemplating air mail service between Saint John and

Halifax? I ask this because the present train service is inadequate and an opportunity is being offered to establish a service by air.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: This matter would be considered in connection with the genera] air mail service, but no decision has been arrived at.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I would like the Postmaster Genera] to consider this matter apart from the general scheme as this is something which is very urgent. It is possible to have such a service established at no great cost and I would appreciate if the minister would give this matter special consideration. The ordinary service has been cut down and the merchants are suffering great hardships. I know the board of trade and other organizations have been pressing this matter, and I ask the minister to give it special consideration.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: It has been discussed by the gentleman who is in charge' of the air service down there and is receiving consideration.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Is it the intention to establish an air mail service between Charlottetown and points in New Brunswick?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I understand there is a service between Moncton and Charlottetown.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Will that be continued?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I hope so.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: What number of postmasters in Canada receive less than $20 per month as commission on stamps?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I have not that information before me, but I can obtain it.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Is there any regulation covering the remuneration of sub-post offices in cities?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: It runs to a maximum of $600 plus certain commissions according to the amount of business done.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Are there any sub-post offices on the outskirts of cities where the only remuneration received is the commission on stamps and postal orders?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: The commission depends upon the amount of business done.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext:
Is the rate of commission set by the department in Ottawa or by the postmaster of the city in which the sub-post office is located?

Farm Rehabilitation-Mr. Bennett

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: The rate is set by the department.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: What would the rate of commission be for a sub-post office located on the outskirts of Hamilton?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: If my hon. friend will look at page 21 of the last report of the Postmaster General, he will find the total revenue for Hamilton and the revenue of the various sub-post offices.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: That does not quite answer my question. I want to know the usual rate of commission.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: That is not shown here, but we can obtain it for my hon. friend.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Could the minister give the rate of commission on stamps paid to village post offices?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: The minimum is $100. Then there is a commission of 70 per cent on the first $1,000. There is 50 per cent on that part of the money order commission collected from the public and included in the revenue from $1,000 to $10,000; there is 30 per cent on the postage stamp revenue from $1,000 to $10,000, and 20 per cent on anything over $10,000.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Would the commission for a post office on the outskirts of a city be as low as two per cent?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: Is my hon. friend talking about stamp vendors or subpostmasters?

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: A sub-post office.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I would not think it would be.

maintopic: CANADA-UNITED KINGDOM TRADE AGREEMENT- INSTRUCTION TO COMMITTEE OP WAYS AND MEANS TO CONSIDER AND REPORT
speechtext: I do not want the minister to think I am trying to hold up his estimates. I shall be glad to take this matter up with him later on.

Item agreed to.
Progress reported.
On motion of Mr. Lapointe (Quebec East) the house adjourned at 10.58 p.m.
